description: The timing_priority_chain family is drafted in full; the other six families carry one exemplar each. The coverage report is the authority on how much exists and what is short per family — this description names no count, because a count written here drifts. Every locator was read off the Core Rules PDF page itself rather than the extracted rules index, which misattributes locators. This is NOT the sixty-question corpus, and the remaining questions are annotated by hand rather than generated in a batch.

questions.question: My attacking unit is in the Backline. Does it contribute Combat Damage this step?
questions.notes: Exemplar. Runs over a closed Combat Showdown built by S-01b: the timing draft states the Combat record, the board states the designated units. First run 2026-09-08 abstained because the minimum state builder had no way to state a Combat; S-01b added that and this question is what it was built to make runnable.

questions.question: I control the Battlefield and my opponent has no units there. Do I score at the scoring step?
questions.notes: Exemplar.

questions.question: My deck is empty and I am about to draw. What happens, and when does the game end?
questions.notes: Exemplar, and a real boundary rather than an invented one: a repeated Burn Out needs the Mode of Play's Victory Score, which the minimum state does not carry, so the engine declines and the answer must abstain with that named reason.

questions.question: It is my main phase and I hold priority. What can I do right now?
questions.notes: Exemplar. bounded_note is required for this family: the enumeration is bounded, complete_action_set is false, and an answer that lists correctly without saying so is still wrong.

questions.question: A unit with an uncompiled ability is on the board. Does its ability change this combat?
questions.notes: Exemplar. A card whose text is not in the snapshot set cannot back a claim, so the answer abstains rather than reasoning from the card name.

questions.question: My opponent drew an extra card by accident in round three. What is the penalty?

zh_hant.question: 第三輪對手不小心多抽了一張牌。罰則是什麼？

questions.notes: Exemplar. This abstention is a decision, not a mechanism running out: the service declines tournament procedure and penalties by policy.

questions.question: Both players have passed once each on a closed chain during my main phase. Does the whole chain resolve, or one item?

zh_hant.question: 我的主要階段，連鎖已封閉，雙方各讓過一次。整個連鎖會一起結算，還是只結算一項？

questions.notes: 340.1 resolves the newest finalized item only; 339.1 is the pass condition that sends the chain to Step 4.

questions.question: I finalized my card onto the chain. Did finalizing it pass priority to my opponent?
questions.notes: 337.1.a: finalizing an item to the chain does not pass Priority.

questions.question: No player holds priority right now. Can either of us take a discretionary action?

zh_hant.question: 現在沒有任何玩家持有優先權。雙方還能做自主行動嗎？

questions.notes: 312.1.b: if no player has Priority, no player can take Discretionary Actions. Measured 2026-09-08 through the real consultation command: the pipeline reached tier A. The engine refused with priority_required and cited Core 312; the precise sub-rule is 312.1.b. My first prediction for this question was C and it was wrong — the engine models the rule.

questions.question: An effect instructs me to make a choice, but I do not hold priority. May I still make it?
questions.notes: 312.1.b.1: players can always take and make choices for Limited Actions when instructed, regardless of Priority. The distinction this question tests is Limited Action against Discretionary Action.

questions.question: A Showdown is open and I just gained Focus. May I play a spell with no Action or Reaction keyword?
questions.notes: 313.2 gives Priority with Focus; 313.1.a's own example refuses a spell without Action or Reaction. Measured 2026-09-08 through the real consultation command: the pipeline reached tier A. The engine refused with action_or_reaction_required_in_showdown, citing Core 313.1 among others.

questions.question: I passed priority during a Showdown. Do I still hold Focus?
questions.notes: 313.3: a player who passes Priority retains Focus. The two are separate, and this question exists because they are easy to conflate.

questions.question: The turn is in a Neutral State. Which player holds Focus?
questions.notes: 313.5: in a Neutral State no player has Focus. Neither player is the answer, not the turn player.

questions.question: I hold Focus but my opponent holds priority. May I take a discretionary action?
questions.notes: 313.4: a player may not make discretionary actions with Focus unless they also possess Priority.

questions.question: The turn is in a Closed State. May I play a card that has no Reaction?
questions.notes: 338.1.a.1: cards and activated abilities cannot be played during a Closed State by default; 338.1.a.2 names Reaction as what makes one legally timed there.

questions.question: My opponent's spell is on the chain and they hold priority. May I play a card right now?
questions.notes: Priority is exclusive (312), and after the chain settles the controller of the newest item gains it (340.4). Measured 2026-09-08 through the real consultation command: the pipeline reached tier A.

questions.question: My chain item finalized and it is a Unit. Does it wait on the chain for a response?
questions.notes: 337.2: a finalized Unit, Gear, or resource-adding ability resolves immediately and moves to Step 4, so there is no window on it.

questions.question: A Showdown just began at a contested Battlefield. Which player gains Focus?

zh_hant.question: 爭奪中的戰場剛開啟對峙。哪一位玩家取得聚焦？

questions.notes: 345: the player who applied Contested status gains Focus. Expected B rather than A: the minimum state builder has no slot for who applied Contested, so the engine has nothing to rule on and the answer is the text. Measured 2026-09-08 through the real consultation command: the pipeline reached tier B. Worth a second look at review: a tier-B run cites the right text without answering 'which player', so the tier alone does not say the question was answered.

questions.question: It is my Beginning Phase and I control a Battlefield my opponent has no units at. Does the scoring step complete and Hold it for me?

correction_record.observed: Run 2026-09-09: the contract expects the scoring step to complete at tier A; the control kernel returned unsupported / mode_unknown — 'the Mode of Play (Victory Score) is not in the state; scoring needs it (456.3, 471.1)'. With the phase set to main instead, the kernel refuses correctly with scoring_step_requires_beginning_phase, so the Beginning Phase draft is right.
correction_record.decided: The engine is right to decline, and the contract stays at A: the rules say the step completes, and rewriting the contract to expect an abstention would hide that the service cannot yet answer a scoring question.
correction_record.follow_up: The minimum state builder has no slot for the Mode of Play, so no Victory Score is in the state and the control kernel declines (mode_unknown, citing Core 456.3). The same absence is what makes the engine decline every Burn Out question. This is a state-builder coverage gap the corpus has now hit from two families; it belongs to a state-builder package, not to S-04.

zh_hant.question: 我的開始階段，我控制一個對手沒有單位的戰場。計分步驟會完成並讓我 Hold 它嗎？

questions.notes: 315.2.b.2 makes Holding every controlled Battlefield the scoring step's task; 469.2 defines Hold as control maintained through the Beginning Phase.

questions.question: Can the victory facts be determined from this position at cleanup?

correction_record.observed: Run 2026-09-09: the contract expects the victory facts to be determined at tier A; the control kernel returned unsupported / mode_unknown — 'the victory facts need the Mode of Play and no teams' (456.3, 472).
correction_record.decided: Same as JC-CS-001: the engine is right to decline, the contract stays at A, and the gap is recorded rather than papered over.
correction_record.follow_up: The minimum state builder has no slot for the Mode of Play, so no Victory Score is in the state and the control kernel declines (mode_unknown, citing Core 456.3). The same absence is what makes the engine decline every Burn Out question. This is a state-builder coverage gap the corpus has now hit from two families; it belongs to a state-builder package, not to S-04.

questions.notes: 472: at a cleanup a player with points at or above the Victory Score and more than any opponent wins. The control step that reads those facts is the claim.

questions.question: I Held a Battlefield this turn and then Conquered it again. Do I score it twice?
questions.notes: 470: a player may only Score, from either method, once per Battlefield per turn. The answer surface has no template for it; declared as debt.

questions.question: I am one point short of the Victory Score and I Conquer a Battlefield. Do I gain the Final Point?
questions.notes: 471.1.b.1: the Final Point through Conquer only if every Battlefield was scored this turn; otherwise the player draws a card instead. Declared as debt.

questions.question: A spell gives me a point while I am one short of the Victory Score. Is that gain held back the way a Conquer is?
questions.notes: 471.1.a.1: points gained from sources that are not Conquer are not beholden to the Final Point restrictions. Declared as debt.

questions.question: Which abilities trigger when I Hold a Battlefield, and can they trigger again the same turn?
questions.notes: 471.2.b: Hold abilities trigger at a Battlefield that was Held; 471.2.c: only when the Battlefield is Scored, so at most once per turn per player. Declared as debt.

questions.question: In what ways can a player gain points in Riftbound?
questions.notes: 194.1.a-d: Holding, Conquering, effects that instruct a gain, and an opponent's Burn Out that picks the player. Declared as debt.

questions.question: My deck is empty during my Draw Phase. Do I still draw after Burning Out?
questions.notes: 315.4.b.1-2: the Turn Player has Burned Out and, after completing it, still Draws 1. The engine declines: a repeated Burn Out needs the Mode of Play's Victory Score, which the minimum state does not carry. A real boundary, expected to abstain.

questions.question: An effect tells me to draw two with one card left in my deck. What happens?
questions.notes: 431.1.a: draw as many as possible, Burn Out, then draw the remaining amount. Same boundary as JC-TSE-001; the engine declines rather than ruling.

questions.question: I Burn Out twice in one turn. Does my opponent gain a point each time?
questions.notes: 431.2.c: to Burn Out, the player chooses an opponent to gain 1 point. The engine declines the repeated Burn Out without a Victory Score; expected to abstain.

questions.question: What is the Victory Score by default, and can anything change it?
questions.notes: 194.3: 8 points by default; 194.3.a: modes or card effects may alter it. Declared as debt.

questions.question: Both of us reach the Victory Score in the same cleanup with the same points. Who wins?
questions.notes: 194.2.a: more points wins; 194.2.b: equal points, play continues until one player has more in a cleanup. Declared as debt.

questions.question: An effect would make me lose a point while I have zero. Do I go negative, and does anything trigger?
questions.notes: 194.4: never below 0; 194.4.a: nothing occurs; 194.4.b: loss triggers do not trigger. Declared as debt.

questions.question: When exactly does the game end after someone reaches the Victory Score?
questions.notes: 194.2: the win is checked in a cleanup; 196: when a player wins, the game ends. Declared as debt.

questions.question: It is my main phase, the chain is empty and I hold priority. What may I do right now?
questions.notes: 410.1.a: a Discretionary Action may be performed at any time during a player's turn in a Neutral Open State. Bounded enumeration; the answer must say so.

questions.question: It is my opponent's turn and nothing is on the chain. Do I have any discretionary action?
questions.notes: 409: a player may only perform actions on their turn unless otherwise specified. Expected: the enumeration for p1 on p2's turn finds a legal action only if one is timed for it; the engine's verdict is the answer.

questions.question: During my main phase, how many discretionary actions may I take?
questions.notes: 316.5.a and 410.1.b: any number, as long as conditions are met and costs paid. Declared as debt.

questions.question: May I take a discretionary action that would leave the game in a forbidden state?
questions.notes: 410.1.b.3, with its own example of a Standard Move onto a Battlefield occupied by two other players' units. Declared as debt.

questions.question: Can I choose to draw a card whenever I want?
questions.notes: 410.2.a-b: a Limited Action is caused by a spell, ability or the turn's progression and cannot be taken at will; drawing is the rule's own example. Declared as debt rather than reusing the 312.1.b.1 template, whose text is a different sentence.

questions.question: Who may play spells during a Neutral Open State?
questions.notes: 316.5.b: only the Turn Player has the ability to play spells or activate abilities in a Neutral Open State. Declared as debt.

questions.question: My opponent holds priority in my main phase. May I play a spell right now?
questions.notes: 312.1.a: only the player with Priority can take Discretionary Actions. Not the enumeration entry: this asks about one action, and the timing kernel rules on it.

questions.question: My spell deals 1 damage to an enemy unit with Shield that is not currently defending. Does Shield reduce it?
questions.notes: 814.1.c: Shield is short for 'While I am a defender, I have +X [M]'; 814.1.d: defender means the Defender designation during Combat. Outside Combat the damage applies as written, and the effect kernel's verdict is the claim.

questions.question: A unit's ability is printed on a card the service has no text for. Does the ability change anything here?
questions.notes: No snapshot, no claim. The answer abstains rather than reasoning from the card's name.

questions.question: A card says Shield with no number. What is its Shield Value?
questions.notes: 814.1.b.3: if X is omitted it is presumed to be 1. Declared as debt.

questions.question: A unit has Shield and is granted Shield 3 by an effect. What is its Shield Value?
questions.notes: 814.2: the Shield Value of all granted Shield keywords is summed; the rule's own example reaches Shield 4. Declared as debt.

questions.question: My unit has Tank. What does Tank require of the player assigning combat damage?
questions.notes: 815.1.b: lethal damage must be assigned to it before any same-controller unit without Tank; 815.1.c.1: still lethal before moving on. Declared as debt.

questions.question: A unit has Tank from two sources. Does it get assigned damage twice over?
questions.notes: 815.2: multiple instances of Tank are redundant. Declared as debt.

questions.question: Does my unit keep its Shield bonus once the Combat it was defending in has ended?
questions.notes: 814.1.d.1: Shield remains in effect as long as the unit maintains the Defender designation. Declared as debt.

questions.question: My opponent's decklist does not match what they are playing. What is the ruling and the penalty?

zh_hant.question: 對手的牌表跟實際打的不一樣。裁決與罰則是什麼？

questions.notes: Declined by policy: tournament procedure and penalties are not the service's to rule on, and this abstention is a decision rather than a mechanism running out.
